git add internal/doctor/doctor.go internal/doctor/doctor_test.go internal/doctor/sandbox.go internal/doctor/sandbox_test.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(doctor): H1/H2/H3/M4 — execution fidelity and honest failure messages

H2: hookInvocationObserved executed the hook via a bare execve, never
matching git's own ENOEXEC fallback to `sh -c '"$0" "$@"'`. A
shebang-less pre-commit — which git runs fine — read as unexecutable
in the sandbox. Now retries through the shell exactly when the direct
exec fails with ENOEXEC, matching git's real invocation. This is not
a uniform sh -c wrap: checkHookPresence still only attempts execution
for a body textscan.IsShellHook already classifies as shell (which
includes "no shebang" — the same case git treats as shell), so a
genuinely non-shell hook is never routed through either path.

H1: when the ethos stub is never reached, hookInvocationObserved used
to collapse every cause into a bare (false, nil) — "stale — run
`ethos enable`", the wrong remedy for a missing interpreter or a hung
host section. classifyMissedInvocation now distinguishes: ENOEXEC/
ENOENT ("could not be executed at all"), a sandbox timeout ("did not
finish within Ns — a chained section may be hanging"), and an
ordinary early exit ("exited N before reaching the ethos call"). A
hook that runs to completion and genuinely never calls ethos still
returns (false, nil) — the one case doctor's existing stale/not-
chained messaging already gets right.

H3: pinned as a regression test — a host section guarding on sandbox-
only state (an empty, freshly git-init'd temp repo) now gets the H1
"exited N before reaching the ethos call" message instead of the
misleading "stale — run `ethos enable`", which fixes nothing in that
case. Five doctor_test.go fixtures that had silently worked around
this exact defect (an undefined `run_lint` command exiting 127) are
switched to the established `true` stand-in convention already used
elsewhere in this file.

M4: hookInvocationObserved now guards on GOOS (via the overridable
sandboxGOOS var, same pattern as sandboxTimeout) and returns
errSandboxUnsupportedPlatform on Windows, before ever touching git or
sh. checkHookPresence turns that into an honest WARN "cannot verify by
execution on this platform" rather than the FAIL every enabled Windows
install would otherwise get on a hook that may be perfectly healthy —
the pre-execution lexical scan was platform-neutral, so silent FAIL
here would be a behavioral regression in the dangerous direction.

Every behavioral change falsified against pre-fix source with its own
regression test (see the added TestHookInvocationObserved and
TestCheckSealHook subtests). `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...`
exits 0. Detached-env gate: 28 ok packages, 0 FAIL.
EOF
)"
